LESSON: ELEMENTS AND COMPOUNDS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements and Compounds
Topic 1.1: Elements and Compounds

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Elements and Compounds
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why is it important to use symbols for representing elements in day-to- day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. explain the relationship between an atom, an element, a molecule and a compound
2. write word equations to represent reactions of selected elements to form compounds

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Elements and Compounds

Teach
• Observe Elements and Compounds in real life (school compound, home, farm).
• Use safe examples only.
• Name → explain → apply.

Worked example
• Fact 1 about Elements and Compounds (in pupil words).
• Fact 2 with a Kenyan example.
• Safe action connected to Elements and Compounds.

Try this
• Draw/label one diagram for Elements and Compounds.
• Write 5 bullet facts about Elements and Compounds.
• Say one safety rule.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• explain the relationship between an atom, an element, a molecule and a compound
• write word equations to represent reactions of selected elements to form compounds

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. List 8 facts on Elements and Compounds.
2. Teach a friend using only bullet points.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet for Elements and Compounds: meaning, diagram, 5 practice questions.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to use symbols for representing elements in day-to- day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• explain the relationship between an atom, an element, a molecule and a compound
• write word equations to represent reactions of selected elements to form compounds

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
